derivation: delta = share_AI * (PoS_AI - PoS_base)/PoS_base. Low: 0.0103*(0.18-0.10)/0.10 = 0.82%. High: 0.0342*(0.18-0.10)/0.10 = 2.74%. claim: Detecting the reported 3-percentage-point Phase II difference between AI-derived and conventional molecules would require about 4,126 molecules per arm; the actual AI Phase II sample is roughly 8 to 10 completions, leaving the comparison about 400-fold underpowered.

figures.denominator_def: two-proportion sample size at alpha=0.05 two-sided, 80% power, p1=0.37, p2=0.40
figures.sample: AI Phase II completions observed: 8 (E-2055); Jayatunga Phase II denominator not disclosed (E-2003)

derivation: n = (z_0.975 + z_0.80)^2 * [p1(1-p1) + p2(1-p2)] / (p2-p1)^2 = (1.96+0.8416)^2 * [0.37*0.63 + 0.40*0.60] / 0.03^2 = 4126 per arm. Observed AI Phase II completions = 8 (E-2055). Ratio 4126/8 = 516x under-powered per arm. Wilson 95% CI on an observed 40% success with n=8 is [15.2%, 71.3%], which contains every plausible industry baseline. Inputs: E-2003, E-2011, E-2055.

claim: At the largest plausible denominator the reported 80-90 percent AI Phase I success rate carries a 95 percent confidence interval that overlaps the conventional industry range, so the Phase I advantage is not established at conventional significance.

figures.denominator_def: Wilson score 95% CI on p=0.85 for candidate denominators n=8, 10, 24, 73
figures.sample: denominator not disclosed by the source (E-2002); computed for n=8 [50.4-96.9], n=10 [54.1-96.5], n=24 [66.1-94.3], n=73 [75.1-91.4]

derivation: Wilson score interval, p=0.85, z=1.96. n=8: [0.504,0.969]; n=10: [0.541,0.965]; n=24: [0.661,0.943]; n=73: [0.751,0.914]. Separately, detecting 55% vs 85% at 80% power needs only ~33 per arm, so the Phase I effect is in principle detectable at n=73 - but only if the AI cohort and the baseline cohort share a denominator definition, which is not demonstrated (E-2002 does not disclose how Phase I 'success' or the comparator denominator were defined). Inputs: E-2002, E-2004, E-2007, E-2055.

Counter-observation: median founding-to-Phase-1 = 6.5 years across 63 AI-native companies (E-2054), and Isomorphic Labs is >4 years from founding with zero registered trials (E-2048, E-2049). The per-programme claim and the organisation-level observation are compatible only if the saved time is reabsorbed elsewhere (platform build-out, target selection, IND-enabling tox, CMC), i.e. discovery-stage compression does not propagate to time-to-clinic. Inputs: E-2008, E-2030, E-2031, E-2048, E-2049, E-2054.

figures.sample: 11.6% from 3,766 designs across 15 targets (E-2020); 68% miniprotein rate from a developer technical report (E-2023)

derivation: ratio = 0.68 / 0.116 = 5.86. Inputs: E-2020 (independent pooled meta-analysis, 3,766 designs), E-2023 (Chai Discovery self-report). The one independent third-party replication located (E-2022, Adaptyv Bio) reproduced 27/32 of a developer's own reported hits, i.e. it validates the reported hits but does not test the denominator of designs attempted, which is where the two rates diverge.
